summary: Configured node1 with a persistent local backend on 127.0.0.1:8091 and nginx reverse proxy on TCP 8090. Both return backend-ready, firewalld exposes only 8090, SELinux remains enforcing, and all services recovered after a verified node reboot.
actions_performed: Created and enabled the backend-8091 systemd service.
Configured persistent SELinux and firewalld policy.
Verified the backend and proxy before reboot.
Restarted node1 exactly once and verified full recovery.

evidence.requirement: Local backend on TCP 8091 returns backend-ready
evidence.summary: The Python backend listens on 127.0.0.1:8091 and returned backend-ready before and after reboot.

evidence.requirement: Reverse proxy publishes the backend on TCP 8090
evidence.summary: Requests to node1's managed IP on port 8090 returned backend-ready through nginx before and after reboot.
Both services are enabled and active; nginx listens publicly on 8090, the backend is loopback-only on 8091, firewalld opens 8090 but not 8091, and SELinux is enforcing.

Healthy baseline boot ID cce73776-a7f7-4f32-b822-95d105c52a64 was captured, the reboot was acknowledged, boot ID changed to bbf155c7-6ed6-44c2-a77d-3ccae604350f, and both services, listeners, firewall policy, configuration, and response data recovered.
